findings.claim: app.multipart(configurer) hands the configurer the very MultipartSettings instance that freeze() later passes to the Dispatcher, and no copy is taken at listen. A configurer that keeps its argument (o -> saved = o) can change maxFileSize/maxRequestSize/maxParts/memoryThreshold/tempDirectory on the running app after listen(), skipping the NEW-state guard, and the plain (non-volatile) fields are read unsafely by worker threads. Static mounts guard against exactly this: DefaultStaticOptions.copy() runs at freeze, and docs/api/static.md says so. Multipart behaves differently from that pattern.
findings.evidence: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/DefaultRestApp.java:202-209 (next is handed to the configurer and stored), :873 (multipartSettings() is passed as-is to the Dispatcher); compare StaticMount.java:35-43 / DefaultStaticOptions.copy()
findings.suggested_fix: Pass multipartSettings().copy() to the Dispatcher in freeze() (one call), and add a test that a captured MultipartOptions changed after listen() does not affect parsing.

findings.claim: The MultipartOptions Javadoc says 'no value means unlimited'. That is wrong: every setting has a bounded default and a bounded range, and docs/api/multipart.md says plainly that unlimited is not allowed. Kotlin and Java users read this Javadoc in the IDE.
findings.evidence: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/MultipartOptions.java:8 vs docs/api/multipart.md ('무제한 설정 허용 여부: 허용하지 않습니다')
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the phrase with 'there is no unlimited value; each setting has the default and range shown on its setter'.

findings.claim: Refactoring stream() into startBody() changed what res.stream(in, null) does. Before wave 6 it failed (isFieldValue(null) threw NPE). Now it commits silently with no Content-Type, because the null check meant for the internal sendBody path also applies to the public stream(). The parameter is non-null under @NullMarked, so Java callers lose fail-fast behaviour. No test pins either behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: In stream(), call Objects.requireNonNull(contentType, "contentType") (closing in first) before delegating, so only sendBody passes null.

findings.claim: FileResponder.respond reads length(), etag() and modified() as three separate resolver calls. Each one repeats the full check(): getCanonicalPath, then one getCanonicalPath per path component in linkFree, then isFile. etag() then stats the file again for its own length and lastModified. A file rewritten during a request can therefore get an ETag that disagrees with the Content-Length and Last-Modified sent next to it, and that wrong ETag gets cached and later answered with 304. For a path of depth d, one static GET makes about 5*(d+2) canonicalisations (open() checks twice) before any byte is sent. That cost matters on Android API 21, which has no canonical cache, and on JVMs run with useCanonCaches=false, as the docs recommend.
findings.suggested_fix: Inside the internal path, take one checked snapshot (length + lastModified from one File after one check) and build the ETag from that snapshot. Leave the public ResourceResolver shape as it is.

findings.claim: app.mimeTypes().register(ext, type) and options.mime(ext, type) only check that type is non-empty. A type containing CR/LF or another control character is accepted at configuration time. It then fails res.header("Content-Type", type) on every request for a matching file, so each of those requests gets a 500 instead of the IllegalArgumentException at registration that other setters give.
findings.suggested_fix: In DefaultMimeTypes.type(), reject a value that is not a valid header field value (the isFieldValue rule), throwing IllegalArgumentException.
